milestones.limitations: Publication event. Task performance does not replace clinical validation.

milestones.limitations: Publication event with provider involvement. Not a prospective clinical study.

milestones.title: AlphaFold 2: Predicting protein structures
milestones.summary: Substantially more accurate protein structures in the CASP14 comparison.
milestones.limitations: Measures structure accuracy, not drug efficacy. Experimental validation and clinical development remain necessary.

milestones.title: AlphaFold 3: Molecular interactions
milestones.summary: Extends prediction to complexes containing proteins, DNA, RNA and small molecules.
milestones.limitations: Stereochemical errors, hallucinated structures and limited representation of dynamics. No clinically validated off-label treatment selection.

milestones.title: Nobel Prize for protein design and structure prediction
milestones.summary: David Baker receives half for computational protein design; Hassabis and Jumper share half for structure prediction.
milestones.limitations: An award establishes neither drug approval nor safe automated care.

milestones.title: ResidencyRL: Learning from simulated patient conversations
milestones.summary: After training, more conversations achieve a diagnostic rubric score of at least 4/5.
milestones.limitations: In-domain evaluation uses an automated rubric related to training. Simulation and evaluator bias; prospective real-world validation is missing.

milestones.title: AI access and unaided learning tests
milestones.summary: Higher immediate knowledge-test scores; the smaller effect after one week remains statistically uncertain.
milestones.limitations: Not a medical population or a long-term deskilling study. Protocol violations affect the immediate test; transfer to health professionals is unproven.

milestones.title: MIRA: Diagnosis and actions in a virtual EHR
milestones.summary: An agent combines simulated history-taking, diagnosis and structured EHR actions.
milestones.limitations: Simulated conversations based on retrospective records. No prospective patient care; generalizability and real-world safety require testing.

pharmaApplications.limit: A connected record alone does not demonstrate fewer medication errors.

pharmaApplications.title: Medication safety

pharmaApplications.limit: Fully automated medication safety has not been established here.

pharmaApplications.limit: No reliable savings estimates are available for this pharmacy setting.

pharmaApplications.limit: Routine local biologic production or automatic off-label selection is not established here.

studies.title: AlphaFold 2: Predicting protein structures
studies.design: Blinded CASP14 structure comparison, 87 protein domains.
studies.summary: Substantially more accurate protein structures in the CASP14 comparison.
findings: Median 0.96 Å versus 2.8 Å for the next-best method. Lower is better.
95% confidence intervals: 0.85–1.16 Å and 2.7–4.0 Å; r.m.s.d. at 95% residue coverage.
studies.relevance: Structure models support hypotheses for drug research.
studies.limitations: Measures structure accuracy, not drug efficacy. Experimental validation and clinical development remain necessary.

studies.title: AlphaFold 3: Molecular interactions
studies.design: Comparison of predicted biomolecular complexes with experimentally determined structures.
studies.summary: Extends prediction to complexes containing proteins, DNA, RNA and small molecules.
findings: One model covers multiple interaction types, improving on the specialized methods tested.
studies.relevance: May support investigation of potential drug binding.
studies.limitations: Stereochemical errors, hallucinated structures and limited representation of dynamics. No clinically validated off-label treatment selection.

studies.title: ResidencyRL: Learning from simulated patient conversations
studies.design: Reinforcement learning with simulated conversations; adversarial in-domain evaluation, n=200 per arm.
studies.summary: After training, more conversations achieve a diagnostic rubric score of at least 4/5.
findings: 88.0% after training versus 81.0% for the base model: +7.0 percentage points.
Trained: 83.5–92.0%; base: 75.5–86.0%. Not a clinical patient-benefit endpoint.
Physician evaluators prefer the trained model in 85 of 97 paired cases (87.6%).
studies.relevance: Studies information gathering and decisions during a conversation.
studies.limitations: In-domain evaluation uses an automated rubric related to training. Simulation and evaluator bias; prospective real-world validation is missing.
studies.sourceDetail: arXiv v1; Table 4, Section 4.5 and Appendix C.7.

studies.title: AI access and unaided learning tests
studies.design: 211 students, 205 at one-week follow-up; GPT-4o access during learning.
studies.summary: Higher immediate knowledge-test scores; the smaller effect after one week remains statistically uncertain.
findings: +7.2 percentage points, p=0.021; intention-to-treat test analysis, n=210.
+3.9 percentage points, p=0.068; n=205. Not significant at the 5% level.
Tutoring and delegation were self-selected. Subgroups cannot establish causal differences between these approaches.
studies.relevance: Informs the design of training for pharmacy teams.
studies.limitations: Not a medical population or a long-term deskilling study. Protocol violations affect the immediate test; transfer to health professionals is unproven.
studies.sourceDetail: Contractor & Reyes, arXiv v2; Tables 4, 7 and A3.

studies.title: MIRA: Diagnosis and actions in a virtual EHR
studies.design: Retrospective MIMIC-IV cases in an EHR sandbox; 574 cases, eight diagnoses.
studies.summary: An agent combines simulated history-taking, diagnosis and structured EHR actions.
findings: 87.8% versus 78.1% for four board-certified physicians, n=311 paired cases; exact McNemar p=0.000287.
studies.relevance: Studies reasoning and actions within a controlled clinical workflow.
studies.limitations: Simulated conversations based on retrospective records. No prospective patient care; generalizability and real-world safety require testing.
studies.sourceDetail: Ferber et al., Nature 655, 1282–1291; Fig. 3a, Methods and Discussion.

trackMilestones.title: Med-PaLM / MultiMedQA
trackMilestones.design: MultiMedQA combines six existing medical question datasets and HealthSearchQA; Flan-PaLM is evaluated through prompting and Med-PaLM is adapted to medicine.
trackMilestones.finding: Flan-PaLM achieves 67.6% on MedQA with four answer options.
trackMilestones.limitations: Not comparable with MedXpertQA, USMLE sample questions or patient benefit. Med-PaLM and Flan-PaLM are different variants. The 12.07.2023 Nature publication belongs to the same study family, not independent confirmation.
trackMilestones.note: Flan-PaLM with four answer options; early preprint version.

trackMilestones.title: ChatGPT: USMLE sample questions
trackMilestones.design: Public USMLE sample questions, excluding images; three prompt formats with explicit handling of indeterminate answers.
trackMilestones.finding: For open-ended questions with indeterminate answers included: Step 1 45.4%, Step 2CK 54.1%, Step 3 61.5%. Claims of passing the USMLE depend heavily on prompting and scoring choices.
trackMilestones.limitations: Not an actual licensing examination or clinical validation. The text reports 350 items, but its subtotals 119+102+122 equal 343; no new aggregate rates or sample sizes are calculated here. Earlier preprint results differ from the final version.
trackMilestones.note: Open-ended questions including indeterminate answers. Not an actual licensing exam.

trackMilestones.title: MedXpertQA v3
trackMilestones.design: Full text test, n=2,450; authors' protocol values already shown in the dashboard.
trackMilestones.finding: GPT-4o-2024-11-20 achieves 30.37% on the full text test.
trackMilestones.limitations: A different, harder benchmark. A lower percentage does not establish regression since 2022/2023; not a patient-benefit study.
trackMilestones.note: A different, harder test. The lower score does not establish regression.

trackMilestones.title: ChatGPT answers: Quality and empathy
trackMilestones.design: 195 Reddit questions; anonymized physician and ChatGPT answers rated by three licensed health professionals each, totaling 585 evaluations.
trackMilestones.finding: Clinical evaluators prefer ChatGPT in 78.6% of ratings (95% CI 75.0–81.8). Empathetic/very empathetic ratings: 45.1% of chatbot versus 4.6% of physician responses.
trackMilestones.limitations: Does not measure patient trust or diagnostic accuracy. Chatbot answers were much longer; evaluators were coauthors, scales were not validated in advance, and there were no clinical endpoints.
trackMilestones.result: AI answer preferred in 78.6% of evaluations
trackMilestones.note: Clinical evaluators, not a patient survey. 195 questions.

trackMilestones.title: GPT-4 access shows no significant physician benefit here
trackMilestones.design: 50 physicians, up to six vignettes; GPT-4 plus conventional resources versus conventional resources alone.
trackMilestones.finding: Median diagnostic rubric score: 76% versus 74%; adjusted difference +2 percentage points, 95% CI −4 to 8, p=0.60.
trackMilestones.limitations: No significant added benefit in the primary comparison and no patient endpoint. Exploratory LLM-only results are not the primary study outcome.

trustContext.title: Early survey: Trust depends on the task
